summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for gastric bypass reversal due to persistent post-bariatric hypoglycemia and bacterial overgrowth. She underwent a successful laparoscopic bypass reversal with no intraoperative complications. Postoperatively, she was managed with epidural and PCA pain control, transitioned to oral hydromorphone as tolerated. The G-tube was used for decompression and clamped on postoperative day 3, with diet advanced to stage III. An upper GI study on postoperative day 1 showed no leak or obstruction. She remained afebrile, hemodynamically stable, and without signs of infection or bleeding. By discharge, she was ambulating independently, tolerating a soft diet, and had pain well controlled. She was discharged home with instructions on diet, wound care, activity restrictions, and close glucose monitoring, including use of glucose gel for hypoglycemia. Follow-up was scheduled for staple removal and surgical evaluation.
